newsitem.title: USA: Englishman rescued after six hours in Hudson River.
newsitem.headline: Englishman rescued after six hours in Hudson River.

text.p: A 73-year-old English tourist spent six traumatic hours clinging to a wooden piling after falling into the chilly waters of New York's Hudson River, police said on Friday.

James Duncalf from Liverpool, northern England, was apparently admiring the view from a wharf in Manhattan when his spectacles fell off the end of his nose. He tried to grab them but lost his balance and fell into the water.
The former scaffolder managed to scramble onto an old jetty piling some 30 feet (nine metres) out into the river, a spokeswoman for the New York Police Department (NYPD) said on Friday.
"He spent six hours on a pier pole until someone saw him and he was then rescued by Harbour Police," said the spokeswoman.
She said Duncalf, who fell into the river at 12th Avenue near West 28th Street, was treated at St Vincent's hospital and later released.
She could not say whether Duncalf spent the six hours in the water or if was able to climb completely clear onto the wooden structure.
No one at the hospital was available to comment on his injuries and the Carlton Hotel where he had been staying during his trip said he had checked out.
